# Attack view (generated by scripts/attack_view.py; do not edit)

Toy parameters: w = 16, 16-bit message digits, 6 chains. 200 independent keys per row, up to 20,000 forgery attempts each.

| what the attacker saw | keys forged | median attempts when forged |
|---|---|---|
| one signature per one-time key | 58 of 200 | 10230 |
| two signatures on one key | 200 of 200 | 17 |

The toy size is deliberately weak: with 16-bit digits even one signature can be brute-forced. The point is the gap between the rows. With the real 256-bit digest, forging from one signature means finding a hash whose 67 digits all dominate the signed ones, which is believed infeasible; a second signature on the same key collapses that margin.
